in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex.

Now I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility:

Are you responsible for Alex's care and upbringing? This means he lives with you, or you contribute towards the cost of looking after him at a rate of at least the amount of Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I'm fully responsible for his care and upbringing. I look after him day to day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for confirming that.

Next question: Is Alex currently in any of the following situations?

1. In full-time non-advanced education (such as primary school, secondary school, or A-levels)
2. In approved training (such as an apprenticeship)
3. Neither of the above

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's 8 years old, so he's in primary school - just doing his regular school classes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for clarifying.

Just a couple more questions:

Do you or your partner (if you have one) currently live in the UK? And are you or your partner a UK national, or do you have the right to live in the UK (such as settled status or indefinite leave to remain)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm a UK national and have the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

One final question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. Here's a summary:

**For Alex:**
- ✅ He is under 16 years old
- ✅ He is in full-time education (primary school)
- ✅ You are responsible for his care and he lives with you
- ✅ You are a UK national living in the UK
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through the High Income Child Benefit Charge. However, it can still be worth claiming to protect your National Insurance record and ensure Alex gets a National Insurance number automatically when he turns 16.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
